# Which role can use which MCP tool

<!-- Generated together with mcp-tool-roles.json; do not edit by hand. -->

An agent has the access of the user it acts for. This page shows what that gives on each role a new
workspace starts with. [rbac-matrix.md](rbac-matrix.md) lists the grants themselves;
[agent-tools.md](agent-tools.md) lists the tools.

Nobody types this page. It is drawn from [mcp-tool-roles.json](mcp-tool-roles.json), and the test that
writes the file fails when the answers change and the file does not. The file's note says how it is
measured:

> Generated by TestTheToolRoleMatrixIsPublished (backend/internal/compose/integration). A passport on each seeded role calls every tool and action once. Each record a call names is one the sweep made through the app's own routes for that role. A 403 counts as a refusal where the admin passes the same call. Any other answer counts as one only where a gate was recorded refusing that role in that call, such as a row it hides as not found. Every other answer fails the test, so every cell is either. Each role whose row scope is narrower than all then calls every tool that takes a company, contact, deal, lead or project on one a colleague owns, and reasons names its answers. Do not edit by hand.

| Mark | Meaning |
|---|---|
| ✓ | The call ran for this role. |
| ✗ | A gate refused this role. |

Row scope, the seat and the passport's scopes still apply to each call. A ✓ says the role passed on a
record it owns; [a colleague's record](#a-colleagues-record) shows what the narrower roles get on one
they do not own.

The sections follow the groups and areas of [mcp-parity.md](mcp-parity.md). A call sits where the
catalog puts the one operation its verb serves. A verb that serves none, or several, is under
[Tools no one operation serves](#tools-no-one-operation-serves).

Regenerate from the repository root, then from `backend/`:

    UPDATE_MCP_TOOL_ROLES=1 make test-it DIR=backend/internal/compose/integration RUN=TestTheToolRoleMatrixIsPublished
    go test ./gates -run TestTheMCPParityCatalogIsPublished -update-mcp-parity

A call that reaches no verdict fails the first command; fix it as
[prove-a-tool-in-the-role-matrix.md](../how-to/prove-a-tool-in-the-role-matrix.md) says.

## What each call needs

tools/list offers a passport a tool, or a router's action, only when its user holds every check below. The checks come from [the tool checks table](../../backend/internal/modules/agents/toolchecks.json), which the same test writes:

> Generated by TestTheToolRoleMatrixIsPublished (backend/internal/compose/integration). Each verb lists the authority checks its admin call was asked, and where a gate refused the admin, the checks of a role that ran it. A verb that picks its record by a kind argument keeps only the checks its call on every kind was asked. A check stays only while no seeded role that lacks it got past it. A tools/list offers an agent a verb only when its user holds every check. Do not edit by hand.

A check is `object.action`, or `object.a|b` for any one of them. `*.action` is the action on any object, `admin` is the admin role key, `scope:team` is a row scope at least that wide, and `scope-narrower-than:all` is a row scope short of all.
